proposals.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381 — Lecture 2: Limit Theorems (Fall 2018)
proposals.use: Finite-variance LLN, scalar/vector CLT statements, probability versus distribution convergence, stochastic orders, Slutsky and first-order delta reasoning. Original chapter proofs/examples must state their own assumptions.
proposals.verification: Actual six-page PDF retrieved and all substantive printed pages 1–5 read; pages 4–5 also rendered locally and visually inspected. Official course identifies instructor and Fall 2018.
proposals.limits: Printed page 4 omits an absolute value in the Op tail definition and omits centering in its sample-mean order example; do not adopt those literal formulas. The source mean-value proof assumes continuous derivative. Use a norm-based stochastic bound and a differentiability remainder proof. General dependence and Lindeberg-Feller extensions are not established by the new chapter merely by citing these notes.

proposals.title: Victor Chernozhukov, MIT 14.385 — Lecture 2: Consistency for Extremum Estimators (Fall 2007)
proposals.use: Separation plus uniform criterion convergence as sufficient conditions for consistency. Chapter will independently prove a finite-dimensional compact approximate-minimizer result and a bounded/Lipschitz finite-net ULLN.
proposals.verification: Actual 23-page PDF retrieved. Read physical pages 10–19 covering compact extremum consistency, proof, identification warning, measurability, pointwise/uniform distinction, ULLN and finite-grid idea. Physical pages 10 and 12 rendered and visually inspected.
proposals.limits: No claim to reproduce or verify all mixing-process, outer-probability, convexity or nonlinear-choice extensions. State measurability/separability explicitly; pointwise consistency across laws is distinct from uniform-in-parameter criterion convergence.

proposals.title: Peter Kempthorne, MIT 18.655 — Lecture 16: Asymptotics, Consistency and Delta Method (Spring 2016)
proposals.use: Consistent plug-in functionals, first-order differentiability remainder and studentized mean. Original exact examples will distinguish weak distributional limits from convergence of moments.
proposals.verification: Actual 33-page PDF retrieved; read slides 3–11 on consistency/plug-ins and slides 22–23 on distributional delta/studentization. Slide 22 rendered and visually inspected.
proposals.limits: Do not adopt uncentered shorthand in the sample-mean bound or claim finite-sample coverage from a limit theorem. No source examples, images or numerical problems reproduced.

proposals.title: David Aldous, Probability Theory (Berkeley C205B/C218B, Spring 2017), notes by Sinho Chewi — Lecture 8, Cramér–Wold device
proposals.use: Direct support for the explicitly invoked finite-dimensional Cramér–Wold characterization; scalar projections identify a joint limit when a matching vector law exists. The chapter derives its scalar-contrast limits and constructs the Gaussian candidate from a covariance square root.
proposals.verification: Actual104-page instructor-hosted PDF retrieved. Read title and printed31–33 (physical32–34): Theorems8.1,8.2,8.4 and Gaussian covariance construction. Printed31/physical32 rendered locally and visually inspected.
proposals.limits: The source reduces the device to a multivariate characteristic-function continuity theorem which is invoked there. This does not amount to a full foundational proof in this chapter. The printed32 tightness display has an n-versus-k sum-index slip; use trace covariance independently. No later Markov/ergodic material read or certified.

scope_limit: Four actually inspected primary scopes. Original chapter proofs, examples and exercises; source cautions documented. No dependent/high-dimensional or uniform-over-model inference is inherited. Source-page rendering is not reader UI QA.
